full_judgment:
2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that the plaintiff earlier instituted Money Suit No. 186 of 1978 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka for realization of sale proceeds of salt and compensation amounting to Tk. 35,31,911/- impleading the defendant-bank and Others. The plaintiff being a reputed businessman and importer, deposited Tk. 7,25,000/- in his Account No. 8514 with the Local Branch of Sonali Bank, Head Office, Dhaka And opened a No. WES/DAC/3/77/134 on 15.08.1977 to import 4000/- Metric Tons of salt from India. Ultimately, he imported 3250 Metric Tons as per bill of landing No. T-2 dated 31.08.1977. The plaintiff requested the Manager, Local Branch, Head Office, Dhaka of Sonali Bank to arrange for clearance and to take delivery of the imported salt. Accordingly, the Local Branch of Sonali Bank, Head Office Dhaka forwarded necessary papers to the Manager, Khulna Branch of Sonali Bank. As per the agreement, the plaintiff was required to deposit Tk. 7,00,000/- in Khulna Branch of the Sonali. Bank to bear all other local expenses. The plaintiff sent his representative, Saleh Ahmed, to deposit Tk. 7,00,000/- in Khulna Branch. On 13.09.1997, the representative of the plaintiff deposited Tk. 7,00,000/- in Khulna Branch for clearing the salt as demanded by the Local Branch of Sonali Bank, Head Office, Dhaka. On receipt of Tk. 7,00,000/-, the Manager, Khulna Branch appointed M/s. Nippon International Traders as the clearing agent for clearance of the imported salt from Chalna Port. The plaintiff instructed the Local Branch of Sonali Bank, Head Office to make delivery of the imported salt to Mr. Saleh Ahmed, against cash payment of Tk. 100 per bag containing 2 mounds of salt and to deposit the sale proceeds in the plaintiff's account. Subsequently, dispute arose, when Khulna Branch most illegally without the consent of the plaintiff sold 233 Metric Tons of salt i.e. 3145 bags at the rate of Tk. 100/- per bag. But out of Tk. 34,30,300/- the defendants deposited Tk. 18,91,000/- in the plaintiff's account and the remaining amount of Tk. 15,39,300/- was not deposited and as such, the plaintiff filed aforesaid Money Suit. 

 8. Defendants contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the suit is barred under Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka, the plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 186 of 1978 which was disposed of. As such, the present suit is also barred by limitation. Instead of filing suit for compensation against the defendants, the plaintiff should have filed such suit against his learned Advocate who gave wrong advice. It is further contended that the suit is not maintainable against any officer of the hank by designation and Sonali Bank which is a body corporate is not a party to the suit and amendment made later would take effect from the date of amendment and as such, the amendment would not save the limitation. The plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 186 of 1978 claiming a sum of Tk. 35,31,901/- on various heads of claim including the present claim of Tk. 7,00,000/- which was barred by the principle of res judicata. The alleged deposit of Tk. 7,00,000/- was not made by the plaintiff but by Mr. Saleh Ahmed and this observation was made by the Commercial Court in Money Suit No. 186 of 1976 and as such the question of depositing Tk. 7,00,000/- by the plaintiff did not arise at all and the alleged claim of Tk. 7,00,000/- in earlier Money Suit No. 186 of 1978 had been disallowed. Making wrong interpretation of the judgment passed by the Appellate Division, the plaintiff has instituted the present suit and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed on the ground of res judicata.
